minutes.headline: Committee approved winter athletic waivers and a warrant article to finance an early-literacy license
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with mothers asking that three young men be added to the Wall of Remembrance, and a task force promoting an opioid forum. Principals gave start-of-year reports, the superintendent updated enrollment and youth sports facility fees, and the athletic director explained eighth-grade waivers. The committee confirmed a new business manager, approved the winter waiver process, voted a warrant article for a special town meeting, accepted donations, and went into executive session.

public_comment.topic: Three mothers asked that their sons be added to the Wall of Remembrance at the AJ Robinson memorial field house.
Mother of Stephen Hamilton asked that the three names be added to the wall.
Representative of the ROAR task force promoted an opioid awareness forum on October 24th at the high school.
Teacher raised policy concerns, deferred to the later policy discussion.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to submit a warrant article for a special town meeting to finance a license of up to five years with Footsteps to Brilliance.
The committee approved the winter athletic waivers under a two-phase process.
The committee appointed James Michael Cassidy as business manager and HR director.
The committee accepted donations, including from the Lions Club and a donor for a lab and sound system.
Mothers asked in public comment that three young men be added to the Wall of Remembrance; the request was referred to the policy list.

why_it_matters: The early-literacy license needs town approval to be financed, so residents at a special town meeting will be asked to vote on a cost the district would share half with United Way over five years.

Youth sports facility fees and gate fees for athletics were discussed, which bear on what families pay for programs and events, and the athletic waiver process decides which eighth graders can join winter teams.
